answer.rationale: The primary contract hard-stops in 14 days with the line at 94% and no buffer, so any action that can interrupt supply is off-limits. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so a negotiate-only or switch bet this cycle is weakly supported and could leave the plant uncovered. memory_c1 is the direct evidence that incumbent renewal kept integration and deliveries intact; memory_c6 (day 65) is the only recent cost lever that does not require a vendor change (longer term / volume pricing). Those two need archive checks before commit. Whether volume pricing can approach the 18% mandate is unknown; c2/c5 are not treated as decisive because a primary cutover or a non-critical month-to-month deferral may not transfer to this unbuffered expiration.
